desk_read: The session split cleanly between energy and everything else. Crude led on both price and commitment: WTI added +2.39% with total open interest rising +22.5k contracts on below-average volume, a new-long read that looks deliberate rather than reactive; Brent matched the tone with +3.42% and flow also flagging new longs, while its backwardation widened to a BZZ26-BZK27 spread of +17.37 $/bbl. Equity index positioning told the opposite story — NQ open interest surged +17.8k contracts on 1.1x average volume into a -2.88% print, a classic new-short flow that leaves the book fragile to any reversal. Gold fell -2.16% while open interest edged higher, a new-short read that warrants watching given how quickly that positioning can become uncomfortable.
oil_read: Both WTI and Brent drew fresh longs yesterday, with total open interest rising +22.5k contracts (+2.0%) in WTI and +2.6k contracts (+2.1%) in Brent, though WTI volume came in at only 0.9x its 20-day average, suggesting the positioning build lacks broad participation. Both curves remain in backwardation; WTI's CLX26-CLJ27 spread holds at +9.29 $/bbl, while Brent's BZZ26-BZK27 spread widened to +17.37 $/bbl (+2.87 on the session).
bias_read: WTI is mildly bullish on fresh longs, though the narrowing backwardation warns of weakening conviction and raises the risk that the move lacks the curve support to sustain itself. Brent shows a cleaner bullish picture, with fresh longs and steepening backwardation reinforcing each other and supporting continuation. On the equity side, both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 carry a mildly bearish bias from new shorts, a positioning setup that supports downside pressure rather than signalling exhaustion. Gold and Silver add to the defensive tilt, each mildly bearish via fresh shorts. Across markets, the overall picture tilts cautiously risk-off, with energy diverging internally and equities and metals aligned on the bearish side.
